subsystems.name: Light source
subsystems.role: supplies the laser light that carries the computation.

subsystems.name: Photonic compute core
subsystems.role: performs matrix multiplication by splitting, phase-shifting and recombining light.
parts: Mach-Zehnder interferometer meshes or microring weight banks

subsystems.name: Electro-optic interface
subsystems.role: converts electronic data into light and back again.

subsystems.name: Weight storage and control
subsystems.role: holds the numbers the mesh multiplies by, and keeps the mesh stable.
parts: electronic memory feeding the phase shifters

subsystems.name: Packaging and optical I/O
subsystems.role: gets light in and out of the chip and joins it to electronics.
parts: fibre arrays and edge or grating couplers

subsystems.name: Software stack
subsystems.role: maps neural networks onto physical light paths.
parts: compiler that places matrix operations on the mesh

buildSteps.title: Design the photonic circuit
buildSteps.detail: Engineers lay out waveguides, splitters and phase shifters in software, simulating how light will interfere so that the mesh computes the intended matrix.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate on silicon-on-insulator wafers
buildSteps.detail: Standard CMOS lithography and etching form nanometre-scale rib waveguides, plus doped regions for modulators and germanium photodetectors.

buildSteps.title: Add active materials
buildSteps.detail: Phase-shifting layers such as silicon nitride, or thin films of lithium niobate or barium titanate, are deposited or bonded to give fast, low-loss tuning.

buildSteps.title: Integrate light sources
buildSteps.detail: III-V laser chips are flip-chip bonded or wafer-bonded to the photonic die, because silicon itself does not emit useful light.

buildSteps.title: Package with electronics
buildSteps.detail: The photonic chip is co-packaged with a driver ASIC, memory and fibre arrays, then actively aligned to sub-micron precision and sealed.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the mesh
buildSteps.detail: Every phase shifter is tuned to route and weight light correctly; closed-loop control cancels the drift caused by temperature changes.

buildSteps.title: Build the system
buildSteps.detail: Converters, memory and host links are added, and the software compiler is used to map a real workload onto the hardware.

buildSteps.title: Test and qualify
buildSteps.detail: Optical, thermal and reliability testing confirms the accelerator can run continuously in a data-centre rack.

prerequisites.why: CMOS-compatible photonic chips are already mass-produced for data-centre transceivers.
they set how fast data can be converted between electrons and photons.
bonding III-V material to silicon works in production, but fully integrated sources remain costly.
weights must persist and be updated cheaply, or the tuning power cancels the optical advantage.
joining photonics and electronics without losing alignment or overheating is the main yield problem.
the converters at the edges are accurate and fast, though they dominate the energy budget.

pathway.milestone: optical transceivers and co-packaged optics inside data centres
pathway.unlocks: proven photonic manufacturing, packaging and fibre-attach supply chains.

pathway.milestone: photonic matrix-multiply accelerators for AI inference in pilot deployments
pathway.unlocks: a demonstration that light can beat electronics on energy per operation for real models.

pathway.milestone: processors with optical compute and optical I/O on the same package
pathway.unlocks: lower power and higher bandwidth between chips, easing the memory bottleneck.

pathway.milestone: optical logic, switching and memory beyond linear algebra
pathway.unlocks: general-purpose optical computing rather than fixed-function accelerators.
